gaps.lead: The journey was so tiring that we slept all day.
gaps.sentence: It was ___ that we slept all day.
gaps.explanation: so tiring (a journey) → such a tiring journey.

gaps.lead: My grandfather planted all these apple trees himself.
gaps.sentence: My grandfather is the ___ all these apple trees.
gaps.explanation: 'the one who…' identifies the agent with a relative clause.

gaps.lead: He had just got home when the power cut happened.
gaps.sentence: ___ home when the power cut happened.

gaps.lead: Do you mind if I come over to see you later?
gaps.sentence: Do you ___ coming over to see you later?
gaps.explanation: 'Have any objection to me/my coming' is the formal equivalent of 'do you mind'.

gaps.lead: I can't wait to see you again.
They won't allow you to enter without a ticket.
gaps.sentence: You ___ to enter without a ticket.
gaps.explanation: 'They won't allow you' becomes 'you won't be allowed'.

gaps.lead: I have never heard such a ridiculous excuse.
gaps.explanation: Fronted 'never' forces inversion: Never have I heard…

gaps.lead: She left early because she didn't want to miss the train.
gaps.explanation: so as not to / in order not to + infinitive.
